performance_intent: Adds a base-ten uint16_t fast path
checked_scope: Public from_chars<uint16_t> on one char16_t, char32_t, or wchar_t code unit; symbolic one-code-unit char16_t parse_int_string error and consumed fields
checker: Alive2 in both directions on exact historical parser IR; native historical public API binaries
compiler: Clang 20.1.8 -std=c++23 -O2, x86-64; libstdc++ 11 headers and library

result.old_to_new: 2 incorrect (error and consumed), 1 failed-to-prove (value: large constant initializer approximated), 0 Alive2 errors
result.new_to_old: 2 incorrect (error and consumed), 1 failed-to-prove (value: large constant initializer approximated), 0 Alive2 errors
result.public_native: For code unit U+0130, old returns invalid_argument, consumes 0, and leaves 123; new succeeds, consumes 1, and writes 0 for char16_t, char32_t, and wchar_t. Plain char '0' matches.

sanitizers: Both historical public witnesses rerun with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and produced the same results without diagnostics
limitations: Counterexample is a non-ASCII code unit, not a valid ASCII decimal digit. No whole-function Alive2 proof for the public API; public difference is shown by historical native binaries and corroborated at the parser boundary. GCC 11 cannot compile the child header because its constexpr function declares a static local, while Clang 20 C++23 builds both. No official historical before/after benchmark score measured.
